title: SHERLOCK: Scheduling Efficient and Reliable Bulk Bitwise Operations in NVMs
problem: Bulk bitwise operations in data-intensive applications suffer from high energy consumption and latency due to data movement between processing and memory subsystems. Efficiently mapping complex applications to CIM-capable NVMs is non-trivial and naive approaches can lead to performance degradation.
motivation: Bulk bitwise operations are critical in databases, web search, cryptography, and image processing where growing data volumes demand energy-efficient and low-latency execution.
method: Sherlock finds the best way to run bulk bitwise operations—like AND, OR, and XOR—directly on special memory chips that can compute data where it sits, rather than shuttling it to a separate processor. It makes two decisions at the same time: where to store data in the memory and what order to execute the operations. By solving these two decisions as one combined problem instead of separately, Sherlock minimizes unnecessary data movement, which reduces both energy consumption and execution time.
key_novelty: Sherlock's core idea is treating data placement and operation scheduling as a single joint problem, rather than two independent ones, for bitwise operations on compute-in-memory hardware.
contributions: Mapping and scheduling method for bulk bitwise operations in CIM-capable NVMs
baselines: prior CIM mapping and scheduling methods
primary_theme: Collaborative scheduling optimization for CIM bulk bitwise operations
